name: Guardian cryptic crossword, Penguin book 3 No 9

book.title: The New Penguin Book of The Guardian Crosswords, volume 3

clue.text: Speak highly of quiet breed

blocks.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
to breed animals is to raise them

explanation.surface: Someone admires a calm, gentle breed of dog or horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise someone is to commend them warmly, a straightforward synonym for talking them up.

clue.text: Specially designed army pool where infants have fun

indicators.note: something specially designed is built to a new plan, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the two words supply the letters

explanation.surface: Soldiers build a custom swimming pool for small children to splash in.
explanation.definitionFit: A playroom is a room set aside in a house for children's games and toys.

clue.text: The eccentric Rainier left in an aeroplane

indicators.note: eccentric means odd and off-centre, so the name that follows is jumbled

blocks.note: the name supplies letters for rearranging
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Prince Rainier of Monaco, shown as a quirky figure, departs on a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: Rainier was the Prince of Monaco; here his name is only letters, with L added to them.
explanation.definitionFit: An airliner is a large passenger aircraft operated by an airline.

clue.text: Some of the most affectionate employees

indicators.note: some of says only part of the following words is needed, read straight through

blocks.note: letters run across the end of most and the start of affectionate

explanation.surface: A boss singles out the warmest, friendliest members of the workforce.
explanation.definitionFit: Staff are the people employed by an organisation, its workforce as a whole.

clue.text: Taking over and doing tap-dancing

indicators.note: dancing feet move about, so the letters before it are moved into a new order

blocks.note: the two words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone steps in to run a show and performs a tap routine too.
explanation.definitionFit: Adopting a child, idea or role means assuming it as your own, a synonym for taking it on.

clue.text: Driver in scene smashed plates and dishes

indicators.note: smashed things are broken into pieces, and the letters before it are reassembled

blocks.note: the three words supply all thirteen letters

explanation.surface: A motorist at a film scene crashes into crockery, breaking it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner service is a matching set of plates, bowls and serving dishes for a meal.

clue.text: Swimmers getting cold and stiff slip back round

indicators.note: going back means the word before it is read right to left
round says the turned word wraps around the other piece

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
stiff and hard are synonyms
taken as written, then turned

explanation.surface: Bathers in icy water grow stiff and slip over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' here means the reversed word is split to wrap the cold-and-stiff piece, not that the swimmers fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilchards are small oily sea fish, and fish are swimmers in crossword language.

clue.text: Design it to take name and number

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so the word before encloses what follows

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A form-filler is told to design something to include a name and number.
explanation.definitionFit: Intent means purpose or aim, as does design in the sense of doing something by design.

clue.text: It's good to stop Elizabeth getting sex!

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
to end something is to stop it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A gossipy exclamation that it would be good to prevent Elizabeth having sex.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth's royal monogram.
explanation.definitionFit: Gender and sex are both used for the male or female category a person belongs to.

clue.text: Roman entrance halls look round at first

indicators.note: turning something round puts its last letter first, so the word before it is read backwards
first tells us the little word at goes at the front of the answer

blocks.note: taken as written
an air is a look or appearance someone has

explanation.surface: A visitor to Rome glances around the grand entrance halls first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' is not a letter selector here: it says the little word at leads, with the turned word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium was the central open hall of a Roman house; atria is the Latin plural.

clue.text: Record weight of something on its own

blocks.note: a single is a record with one song
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A query about how heavy a solitary item on a record is.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is an individual item standing apart, such as a lone card in a suit or an only child.

clue.text: Source of illumination for exotic dancers?

definitions.text: Source of illumination for exotic dancers?

blocks.note: surface reading: a light source, such as fluorescent tubes
setter's reading: exotic dancers are strippers, so their lights could be called stripper lights

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a strip of tube lights is read as lighting for striptease.
explanation.definitionFit: Strip lighting is fluorescent tube lighting fitted in long strips along a ceiling.

clue.text: Strengthen something that controls power

blocks.note: a rein controls a horse
force is power or strength

explanation.surface: A neat description of a device that regulates energy and makes things stronger.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce a wall or argument is to add support and make it sturdier.

clue.text: In future ring off once man's gone ahead

indicators.note: a ring is the round letter, and off says take it away from the next word
having gone ahead, this piece sits in front of what remains

blocks.note: he is a man, the possessive standing for 'man is'
taken as written before its ring is lost

explanation.surface: A telephone call is ended once a man has gone on ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring off' reads as hanging up the phone, but a ring is the round letter O, removed from the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hence can mean from this time on, as in 'two years hence', a point in time yet to come.

clue.text: Too much publicity concerning lack of shelter

blocks.note: over means about, as in a row over money
exposure is being left unprotected from the weather

explanation.surface: A celebrity complains of media attention that leaves them with nowhere to hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Overexposure describes an excess of media coverage, so that the public grows tired of a person.

clue.text: Cooked meal then includes many a cheese

indicators.note: cooked food is altered from its raw state, so the following words are rearranged
includes means the jumbled words hold another piece inside them

blocks.note: letters to rearrange
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: A prepared meal then includes a great many cheeses.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmenthal is a Swiss cheese, holey and pale yellow, named after a valley near Bern.

clue.text: Men face going topless for picture

indicators.note: going topless means losing the top, the first letter of the word

blocks.note: taken as written, before losing its head
visage is a literary word for the face

explanation.surface: Men posing shirtless for a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' points at the first word, Men, which loses its M; face is left whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To envisage something is to imagine it, to picture it in the mind.

clue.text: Delayed when fed up, made a mistake

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone, sick of it all, slipped up and was held up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' looks like the idiom for annoyed, but it is fed written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Deferred means postponed, put off until a later time.

clue.text: At all times everywhere state I'm no stranger to personal influence

indicators.note: made stranger, the preceding words become odd and so are rearranged

blocks.note: letters of the phrase to be rearranged
presence is the impressive personal bearing that sways others

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being well acquainted with charisma and its effects.
explanation.definitionFit: Omnipresence is the condition of being present in every place, a quality attributed to God.

clue.text: When long way in front gets sudden pain

indicators.note: in front places the second piece at the head of the answer

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: A runner far ahead of the field gets a sudden cramp.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sharp pain in the side, often brought on by running.

clue.text: It takes five to get a rule changed, one estimates

indicators.note: changed means the words before it are altered into a new order

blocks.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A committee reckons it needs five votes to alter a regulation.
explanation.definitionFit: A valuer is a professional who assesses what property or goods are worth.

clue.text: Skill when reversing in coach

indicators.note: reversing makes the word before it run the opposite direction

blocks.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
taken as written

explanation.surface: A driver needs skill when backing a coach into a space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' suggests a bus in the surface, but it is the verb meaning to instruct.
explanation.definitionFit: To train someone is to teach and drill them, just as a sports coach does.

clue.text: Hinged clasp for attaching to locks

definitions.text: Hinged clasp for attaching to locks

blocks.clueFragment: Hinged clasp for attaching to locks
blocks.note: surface reading: a hasp or fastening fitted to door or padlock hardware
setter's reading: locks are tresses of hair, and the clasp holds them in place

explanation.walkthrough: Locks reads as the things keys open; here they are strands of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair slide is a decorative clip, often hinged, that holds hair in position.

clue.text: Stores having no time for hosiery

indicators.note: having no means the named letter is taken away

blocks.note: stocks are stores or supplies of goods
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Shops too busy to deal with stockings and tights.
explanation.definitionFit: Socks are knitted coverings for the feet, a category of hosiery.

clue.text: People queueing dash in front of boundary at ball game

indicators.note: in front of says the second piece leads and the first follows

blocks.note: a touch is a small amount, a dash of something
people queueing form a line

explanation.surface: A queue of spectators makes a rush for the front of the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: In football and rugby the touchline is the side boundary marking the edge of the playing field.

clue.text: Companion to warm and dry seat

blocks.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
to air laundry is to warm and dry it

explanation.surface: Instructions to a friend on warming and drying a damp seat.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is Companion of Honour, an honour awarded by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair is a piece of furniture people sit upon, an everyday kind of seat.

clue.text: One has to provide time for this work

definitions.text: One has to provide time for this work

blocks.clueFragment: One has to provide time for this work
blocks.note: surface reading: a busy person must set aside hours for a demanding job
setter's reading: the work literally produces timekeepers, the clocks and watches that tell the time

explanation.walkthrough: Making time for something usually means scheduling; here it means building the instruments that show it.
explanation.definitionFit: Horology is the craft and science of making clocks and measuring the passing of hours.

clue.text: Very big nurse wanted port

blocks.note: OS is outsize, a clothing size label
to nurse a patient is to tend them

explanation.surface: A hospital advertises for an exceptionally large nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a Belgian seaport on the North Sea coast with ferry links to England.
